title: Clinical Performance Measures for Stroke Rehabilitation: Performance Measures From the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association
shortTitle: Clinical Performance Measures for Stroke Rehabilitation

recommendations.section: Performance Measure 1: Enteral Feeding (Preventive Treatment; acute hospital)
recommendations.text: People with stroke who cannot safely swallow should have enteral feeding initiated within 7 d after stroke. Measured as: "Enteral Feeding: Percentage of people with stroke with swallowing difficulties or barriers to oral feeding who have enteral feeding initiated within 7 d after stroke." Numerator: people with stroke unable to safely swallow who have had enteral feeding initiated within 7 d after stroke. Excluded: people placed on end-of-life care during the first 7 d after stroke; people who died or were transferred during the first 7 d after stroke. Period of assessment: day 7 after presentation at acute care.

recommendations.section: Performance Measure 2: Assessment of Urinary Retention (Preventive Treatment; acute hospital, postacute facility)
recommendations.text: People with stroke and urinary symptoms should have an assessment of urinary retention through bladder scanning or intermittent catheterizations after voiding while recording volumes. Measured as: "Urinary Retention: Percentage of people with stroke with incontinence or urinary retention who received assessment of bladder residuals." Excluded: people with indwelling Foley catheters or other forms of nonphysiological bladder drainage; people with normal spontaneous voiding without incontinence or retention. Period of assessment: during acute hospitalization; during postacute rehabilitation unit stay or SNF.

recommendations.section: Performance Measure 3: Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility (Treatment Standards/Disposition Process; acute hospital, postacute facility)
recommendations.text: People with stroke who qualify for, would benefit from, and have geographic access to IRF care should receive acute inpatient rehabilitation in an IRF. Measured as: "IRF Referral: Percentage of people with stroke who qualify for, would benefit from, and have geographic access to IRF care who are transferred to an IRF for rehabilitation." Included: hospitalized people with acute stroke who require active ongoing intervention of multiple rehabilitation therapy disciplines, can participate in and benefit from >=3 h of rehabilitation therapy per day, require physician supervision during rehabilitation, and require a coordinated interdisciplinary team approach. Excluded: death before hospital discharge; limited rehabilitation potential or inability to tolerate an intensive program because of frailty or comorbidities; no geographic access to an IRF; patient, family, or health care proxy declines IRF admission. Period of assessment: discharge from acute hospital stay after stroke.

recommendations.section: Performance Measure 4: ADL and Mobility (Active Treatment Process; acute hospital, postacute facility, home care, outpatient)
recommendations.text: People with stroke should receive ADL and mobility training tailored to individual needs and eventual discharge setting. Measured as: "ADL: Percentage of people with stroke who receive ADL and mobility training tailored to individual needs and eventual living situation." People with stroke receiving end-of-life care are excluded from the compliance calculation.

recommendations.section: Performance Measure 5: Aphasia — Speech and Language Therapy (Active Treatment Process; acute hospital, postacute facility, home care, outpatient)
recommendations.text: People with stroke with residual aphasia should receive SLT (speech and language therapy). Measured as: "SLT for Aphasia: Percentage of people with stroke with aphasia who receive SLT."

recommendations.section: Performance Measure 6: Education About Impact of Stroke (Educative Treatment Process; acute hospital, postacute facility, home care, outpatient)
recommendations.text: People with stroke should be provided education about stroke, including information on secondary prevention, rehabilitation, and the opportunity to talk about the impact on their lives. Measured as: "Patient Education: Percentage of people with stroke provided with education about stroke: information, advice, and the opportunity to talk about the impact on their lives."

recommendations.section: Performance Measure 7: Fall Prevention (Active and Preventive Treatment Process; acute hospital, postacute facility, home care, outpatient)
recommendations.text: People with stroke who have impaired balance, low balance confidence, or fear of falls should be provided a fall prevention training program. Measured as: "Fall Prevention: Percentage of people with stroke at risk for falls provided with a fall prevention training."

recommendations.section: Performance Measure 8: Poststroke Depression Screening (Assessment; acute hospital, postacute facility, home care, outpatient)
recommendations.text: People with stroke should be screened for depression with a structured depression inventory. Measured as: "Poststroke Depression Screening: Percentage of people with stroke who receive a structured depression assessment inventory."

recommendations.section: Performance Measure 9: Poststroke Depression Treatment (Treatment; acute hospital, postacute facility, home care, outpatient)
recommendations.text: People with stroke diagnosed with poststroke depression should receive appropriate evidence-based treatment. Measured as: "Poststroke Depression Treatment: Percentage of people with stroke diagnosed with depression who receive treatment for depression" (per patient population: percentage receiving antidepressant therapy or evidence-based psychotherapy).

recommendations.section: Performance Measure 10: DVT Prophylaxis (Preventive Treatment; postacute facility)
recommendations.text: People with stroke who have impaired mobility should receive DVT prophylaxis during postacute inpatient rehabilitation. Measured as: "Prevention of DVT: Percentage of people with stroke who have impaired mobility who receive some form of DVT prophylaxis during postacute inpatient rehabilitation" — for all the days that they were at risk, before regaining mobility, without contraindications.

recommendations.section: Performance Measure 11: Postacute Rehabilitation (Treatment Standards/Disposition Process; postacute facility)
recommendations.text: People with stroke receiving postacute rehabilitation in an inpatient setting should receive organized, coordinated, interprofessional care. Measured as: "Organization of Postacute Rehabilitation Care: Percentage of people with stroke who are candidates for postacute rehabilitation and who receive organized, coordinated, interprofessional care."

recommendations.section: Performance Measure 12: Follow-Up After Discharge (Assessment Process; home care, outpatient)
recommendations.text: Follow-up is recommended to ensure that people with stroke and their families receive the necessary rehabilitation services after discharge. Measured as: "Follow-Up: Percentage of people with stroke discharged to home who receive the necessary rehabilitation services after discharge."

recommendations.section: Performance Measure 13: Tailored Exercise and Fitness Program (Active Treatment Process; outpatient)
recommendations.text: People with stroke should be provided an individually tailored exercise and fitness program. Measured as: "Exercise: Percentage of people with stroke discharged home who are provided an individually tailored exercise and fitness program" — an individually tailored exercise program to enhance cardiorespiratory fitness and to reduce the risk of stroke recurrence, provided after successful screening.
